sentences.zh: 他在柏林待了一个月，最后绝望到拿出了他随身带来的埃尔舍帽子。

sentences.en: And he puts it on his head and kind of stands in a prominent place when Frederick the Great is on parade, hoping that Frederick the Great will see it and take an interest in it.
sentences.zh: 他把它戴在头上，站在显眼的地方，当腓特烈大帝阅兵时，希望腓特烈大帝能看到它并产生兴趣。

sentences.en: And Frederick does notice it, but doesn't like it.
sentences.zh: 腓特烈确实注意到了，但并不喜欢它。

sentences.en: He's surely not tall enough for Frederick the Great and not sufficiently interested in military parades.
sentences.zh: 他肯定不够高，入不了腓特烈大帝的眼，而且对军事阅兵也不够感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think that we've said that Boswell's face is not that of a man who's interested in military parades.
sentences.zh: 我想我们说过，鲍斯韦尔的脸看起来就不像是一个对军事阅兵感兴趣的人。

sentences.en: No, definitely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: Which is also another reason why it's very lucky for him.
sentences.zh: 这也是他很幸运的另一个原因。

sentences.en: I think he didn't get into the guards.
sentences.zh: 我想他没能进入卫队。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Hopelessly ill-suited to it.
sentences.zh: 完全不适合干那个。

sentences.en: Once he's finished faffing around in Germany, you might think, well, it's time to go back to Scotland or indeed to London to see Dr. Johnson again.
sentences.zh: 一旦他在德国折腾完了，你可能会想，是时候回苏格兰或者伦敦再见约翰逊博士了。

sentences.en: But no, he goes on, doesn't he, to Switzerland because now he's in his celeb hunting vein.
sentences.zh: 但没有，他继续前行了，不是吗？去了瑞士，因为他现在正处于追星模式。

sentences.en: And there's, well, there's a couple of celebrities in particular.
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，有几位名人特别值得关注。

sentences.en: And one of these people is one of the worst men who's ever lived.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人是有史以来最糟糕的人之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's Jean-Jacques Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 没错，是让-雅克·卢梭。

sentences.en: Jean-Jacques Rousseau is the first of these two celebrities that Boswell's going to meet.
sentences.zh: 让-雅克·卢梭是鲍斯韦尔即将见到的这两位名人中的第一位。

sentences.en: Like Johnson, he's more than a celebrity.
sentences.zh: 像约翰逊一样，他不仅仅是一位名人。

sentences.en: He's a great moraliSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位伟大的道德家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Or at least, so it seems at this point, he's also a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 或者至少在这一点上看起来是这样，他也是一位哲学家。

sentences.en: He's a noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位小说家。

sentences.en: He has very novel views on sex, on religion, on society, particularly on education.
sentences.zh: 他对性、宗教、社会，特别是教育，有着非常新颖的观点。

sentences.en: He's very, very keen on the notion that parents should take good care of their children and bring them up responsibly.
sentences.zh: 他非常、非常推崇父母应该照顾好孩子并负责任地抚养他们的观念。

sentences.en: And for all of these reasons, I think Boswell, as he had done when he arrived in London, is looking for someone who can provide him with moral guidance.
sentences.zh: 基于所有这些原因，我想鲍斯韦尔就像他刚到伦敦时一样，正在寻找一个能为他提供道德指导的人。

sentences.en: And so he goes to the village where Rousseau is living and he writes to him begging for a meeting.
sentences.zh: 于是他去了卢梭居住的村庄，写信恳求见面。

sentences.en: And Rousseau replies, I am ill, in pain, really in no state to receive visits.
sentences.zh: 卢梭回复说，我病了，很痛苦，实在没有状态接待访客。

sentences.en: Yeah, you'd expect that from him.
sentences.zh: 是啊，你对他会有这种预期。

sentences.en: And this would probably put most people off, but it doesn't put Boswell off.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让大多数人望而却步，但并没有让鲍斯韦尔退缩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, he turns up at the door.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他直接出现在了门口。

sentences.en: Rousseau's housekeeper, who inevitably is also his mistress, in fact, has given him five children, comes down the stairs.
sentences.zh: 卢梭的管家，不可避免地也是他的情妇，事实上还为他生了五个孩子，走下楼梯。

sentences.en: She's a French woman called Thérèse Le Vasseur.
sentences.zh: 她是一位名叫特蕾莎·勒瓦瑟的法国女性。

sentences.en: But Boswell absolutely charms her, sweet talks her into allowing her in.
sentences.zh: 但鲍斯韦尔完全迷住了她，甜言蜜语地让她放他进去。

sentences.en: He goes upstairs and there is Rousseau sitting in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 他上了楼，卢梭正坐在厨房里。

sentences.en: And Rousseau is famously grouchy and he periodically tries to get rid of Boswell by saying that he needs to use his chamber pot.
sentences.zh: 卢梭以脾气暴躁著称，他时不时地试图通过说自己需要用便壶来打发走鲍斯韦尔。

sentences.en: But Boswell, oh, don't stand on ceremony with me.
sentences.zh: 但鲍斯韦尔说，噢，别跟我客气。

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 继续吧。

sentences.en: Crack on.
sentences.zh: 继续吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, don't worry about me.
sentences.zh: 行，别担心我。

sentences.en: But basically, Boswell is not remotely put off by Rousseau needing to use his chamber pot at all, hangs around.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，博斯韦尔完全没被卢梭需要用尿壶这件事给吓跑，反而赖着不走。

sentences.en: And Rousseau ends up being completely charmed by him.
sentences.zh: 而卢梭最终也被他彻底迷住了。

sentences.en: And they do end up having a series of really quite lengthy chats over the course of five days.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的五天里，他们确实进行了一系列相当冗长的谈话。

sentences.en: And this, for biographers of Rousseau, is an incredible resource.
sentences.zh: 对于卢梭的传记作者来说，这简直是不可思议的宝贵资料。

sentences.en: So Peter Martin, who's written the definitive biography of Boswell, says that Boswell's account of Rousseau's speech is accepted as the most vivid known to exiSt.
sentences.zh: 彼得·马丁写过博斯韦尔的权威传记，他说博斯韦尔对卢梭言谈的记录被公认为现存最生动的版本。

sentences.en: Boswell, I mean, if he'd had a smartphone, he would so have recorded it all and put it on social media.
sentences.zh: 我是说，博斯韦尔要是当时有智能手机，他绝对会把这一切都录下来发到社交媒体上。

sentences.en: And that's effectively what he's doing with, you know, he talks to Rousseau, he rushes back to his inn, he writes it all up.
sentences.zh: 他当时做的其实就是这样——他跟卢梭谈话，然后冲回旅馆，把一切都记下来。

sentences.en: And so there you have what is the closest we will ever have to a recording of Rousseau's conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我们所能拥有的最接近卢梭谈话录音的东西了。

sentences.en: And Boswell is deliriously happy about this.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔对此感到欣喜若狂。

sentences.en: And again, there's this sense when he writes it up in his journal of kind of watching himself as the hero of his journal.
sentences.zh: 而且，当他在日记中写下这些时，又有一种他在审视自己作为日记主角的感觉。

sentences.en: So he writes, gods, am I now then really the friend of Rousseau?
sentences.zh: 于是他写道：天哪，难道我现在真的是卢梭的朋友了吗？

sentences.en: I suppose the parcel of young fellows saying, come Boswell, you'll dine with us today.
sentences.zh: 我猜那一群年轻人会说：来吧博斯韦尔，今天跟我们一起吃饭。

sentences.en: No, gentlemen, excuse me, I'm engaged.
sentences.zh: 不，先生们，抱歉，我有约了。

sentences.en: I dine today with Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 我今天要和卢梭共进晚餐。

sentences.en: Oh, the sense of pride is so comical, but I think so engaging.
sentences.zh: 噢，这种自豪感真是既滑稽，又让人觉得很有趣。

sentences.en: And if there's one person, I mean,
sentences.zh: 如果说有一个人，我是说，

sentences.en: there's probably only one person who's even more famous than Rousseau among Francophone philosophers and wits and sort of scholars and thinkers and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 在法语世界的哲学家、才子、学者和思想家之类的人中，可能只有一个人比卢梭更出名。

sentences.en: And that is Voltaire.
sentences.zh: 那就是伏尔泰。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And once again, Boswell, I mean, we don't have the chamber pot trick, but Boswell basically talks himself into Voltaire's company, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 又一次，博斯韦尔——虽然我们没有尿壶那样的桥段，但博斯韦尔基本上是靠口才让自己挤进了伏尔泰的圈子，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Voltaire's just down the road from Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 是啊，伏尔泰住的地方离卢梭不远。

sentences.en: He's in Switzerland as well.
sentences.zh: 他也住在瑞士。

sentences.en: And again, Boswell turns up.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔又一次找上门去了。

sentences.en: He's told, no, Monsieur Voltaire doesn't want to see you.
sentences.zh: 他被告知：不，伏尔泰先生不想见你。

sentences.en: Boswell hangs around.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔就在那儿磨蹭。

sentences.en: Eventually, Voltaire comes down in his dressing gown.
sentences.zh: 最终，伏尔泰穿着睡袍下来了。

sentences.en: Boswell pounces on him.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔立刻扑了上去。

sentences.en: And again, Voltaire is kind of seduced by Boswell's charm.
sentences.zh: 伏尔泰也再次被博斯韦尔的魅力所折服。

sentences.en: And again, Boswell writes it up in such a kind of entertainingly self-regarding way.
sentences.zh: 而博斯韦尔又以一种极其自恋且有趣的方式把这些写了下来。

sentences.en: Monsieur de Voltaire and I remained in the drawing room with a great Bible before us.
sentences.zh: 伏尔泰先生和我坐在客厅里，面前放着一本大圣经。

sentences.en: And if ever two mortal men disputed with vehemence, we did.
sentences.zh: 如果说有两个凡人曾激烈争论过，那一定就是我们。

sentences.en: Yes, upon that occasion, he was one individual and I another for a certain portion of time.
sentences.zh: 是的，在那一刻，在某段时间里，他是他，我是我。

sentences.en: There was a fair opposition between Voltaire and Boswell.
sentences.zh: 伏尔泰和博斯韦尔之间进行了一场公平的较量。

sentences.en: It would be interesting to hear Voltaire's version of that conversation to see if it was exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 如果能听到伏尔泰对那次谈话的版本，看看是否完全一致，那会很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, the context for this is that Voltaire is the most famous infidel in Europe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，背景是伏尔泰是欧洲最著名的异教徒。

sentences.en: And Boswell is turning up and casting himself as, you know, the person who's going to convert Rousseau back to orthodoxy and so on.
sentences.zh: 而博斯韦尔找上门来，把自己塑造成一个要让卢梭回归正统的人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And again, I think it's so revealing about exactly why Boswell loves meeting these great men.
sentences.zh: 我再次认为，这非常深刻地揭示了博斯韦尔为什么喜欢结识这些伟人。

sentences.en: It's not just about celebrity.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是为了名气。

sentences.en: It's about getting moral guidance of people who he recognises are much profounder, much more brilliant thinkers than he is actually in his heart of hearts.
sentences.zh: 这是为了从那些他内心深处承认比自己更深刻、更卓越的思想家那里获得道德指引。

sentences.en: So I think there is an element of self-mockery in that description of Voltaire and Boswell being intellectual equals.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，他在描述伏尔泰和博斯韦尔是智力上的平等对手时，带有一种自嘲的成分。

sentences.en: And while this has been going on, his father, Lord Affleck, has been pestering him, saying, what on earth are you doing?
sentences.zh: 而当这一切发生时，他的父亲阿弗莱克勋爵一直在烦他，问他到底在干什么？

sentences.en: You were meant to come home after you finished your studies and you trekked and you're going further and further away from Scotland, not towards it.
sentences.zh: 你本该在学业结束后回家的，结果你到处游荡，离苏格兰越来越远，而不是越来越近。

sentences.en: And Voltaire and Rousseau, I mean, these are not the kind of people that a Scottish Presbyterian Whig would in any way approve of.
sentences.zh: 伏尔泰和卢梭，这些人可不是苏格兰长老会辉格党人会认可的类型。

sentences.en: And so he is absolutely saying to Boswell, come home now.
sentences.zh: 所以他绝对是在对博斯韦尔说：现在就回家。

sentences.en: And Boswell predictably completely ignores it because there is one further celebrity he's going to meet.
sentences.zh: 而博斯韦尔不出所料地完全无视了，因为他还要去见最后一位名人。

sentences.en: And this is going to be the most incredible drama of all.
sentences.zh: 这将是最不可思议的一出大戏。

sentences.en: So from Switzerland, Boswell goes to Italy where he, as we will see, misbehaves himself very badly.
sentences.zh: 所以从瑞士，博斯韦尔去了意大利，正如我们将要看到的，他在那里表现得非常糟糕。

sentences.en: And then from Italy, he sets sail for Corsica.
sentences.zh: 然后从意大利，他启程前往科西嘉岛。

sentences.en: And almost everybody tells him, you are mad to be going there.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有人都告诉他：去那里简直是疯了。

sentences.en: So the Corsicans are in the throes of an independent struggle against Genoa, who is the imperial mistress.
sentences.zh: 当时科西嘉人正处于反抗热那亚——也就是他们的帝国女主人——的独立斗争中。

sentences.en: So there's, you know, lots of guns going off all over the place.
sentences.zh: 所以到处都是枪声。

sentences.en: And that's what Corsica is like anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正科西嘉就是那样。

sentences.en: People are always firing guns in Corsica, even if they're not in a war.
sentences.zh: 科西嘉人总是开枪，即使不在战争时期也是如此。

sentences.en: It's just a very, very violent place.
sentences.zh: 那地方非常、非常暴力。

sentences.en: And on the crossing, there are kind of Corsican sailors and they tell Boswell, any attempt to debauch a Corsican woman will result in instant death.
sentences.zh: 在横渡海峡时，那些科西嘉水手告诉博斯韦尔：任何试图调戏科西嘉女人的行为都会导致当场死亡。

sentences.en: So this is something that Boswell, to give him credit.
sentences.zh: 所以，这一点博斯韦尔倒是听进去了，值得表扬。

sentences.en: That's bad news for Boswell.
sentences.zh: 这对博斯韦尔来说是个坏消息。

sentences.en: He does take on board.
sentences.zh: 他确实记住了。

sentences.en: So he lands.
sentences.zh: 他登陆了。

sentences.en: He knows that if he even so much as looks as a woman, he's going to get, you know, killed.
sentences.zh: 他知道如果他哪怕多看女人一眼，他就会被杀掉。

sentences.en: So that's alarming.
sentences.zh: 这太吓人了。

sentences.en: And then he has to make a very perilous journey across wild, mountainous, rocky country to join the freedom fighters.
sentences.zh: 然后他必须穿越荒凉、多山、岩石遍布的土地，进行一段非常危险的旅程，去加入那些自由战士。

sentences.en: But Boswell absolutely loves it.
sentences.zh: 但博斯韦尔对此乐此不疲。

sentences.en: He admires the primitive character of the Corsicans, which he identifies with the virtue of the ancient Greeks and Romans.
sentences.zh: 他钦佩科西嘉人原始的性格，并将其与古希腊人和罗马人的美德联系起来。

sentences.en: And the chief object of this kind of hero worship of the Corsicans is the general who is leading the Corsican fight for independence.
sentences.zh: 而这种对科西嘉人的英雄崇拜的主要对象，是领导科西嘉独立斗争的将军。

sentences.en: And this is Pasquale Paoli.
sentences.zh: 这就是帕斯夸莱·保利。

sentences.en: So we talked about him in our episode about the young Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 我们在关于年轻拿破仑的那一集里谈到过他。

sentences.en: So back in the days when Napoleon had a Corsican sort of Genoese style accent, he was greatly enamoured of this guy, Paoli, who left a massive shadow, not just over Corsica,
sentences.zh: 在拿破仑还带着科西嘉那种热那亚口音的日子里，他非常迷恋这个保利，保利不仅在科西嘉，

sentences.en: but actually over Europe.
sentences.zh: 实际上在整个欧洲都留下了巨大的阴影。

sentences.en: He was the kind of Che Guevara, the romantic folk hero of the late 18th century, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 他就像是18世纪末的切·格瓦拉，那种浪漫的民间英雄，对吧？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是。

sentences.en: He is possibly the kind of the most admired political figure in Europe in this stretch of the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 他可能是18世纪这一时期欧洲最受推崇的政治人物。

sentences.en: And Boswell plays a key role in promoting him as that, because Boswell thinks Paoli is amazing.
sentences.zh: 而博斯韦尔在宣传他方面发挥了关键作用，因为博斯韦尔认为保利太了不起了。

sentences.en: And actually, he hero-worships Paoli even more than he hero-worships Johnson, because he associates Paoli, again, with kind of ancient history.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他崇拜保利甚至超过了崇拜约翰逊，因为他再次将保利与古代历史联系在一起。

sentences.en: He sees him as someone stepped from the pages of Plutarch or something.
sentences.zh: 他视他为从普鲁塔克书中走出来的人物。

sentences.en: And he describes Paoli, he's a tall, strong, and well-made, of a fair complexion, a sensible, free, and open countenance, and a manly and noble carriage.
sentences.zh: 他这样描述保利：身材高大、强壮、匀称，肤色白皙，神情明智、自由、开朗，举止刚毅而高贵。

sentences.en: This is a man who is fighting for freedom, who's laid his life on the line.
sentences.zh: 这是一个为自由而战，将生命置之度外的人。

sentences.en: And Boswell is all over this.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔完全被迷住了。

sentences.en: Now, Paoli is completely bewildered by Boswell.
sentences.zh: 现在，保利对博斯韦尔感到非常困惑。

sentences.en: Boswell is the first hero-worshipper that Paoli has met.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔是保利见过的第一个英雄崇拜者。

sentences.en: And he can't fathom why Boswell has turned up.
sentences.zh: 他无法理解博斯韦尔为什么会出现在这里。

sentences.en: But as with Rousseau, as with Voltaire, his suspicions are gradually melted by Boswell's charm.
sentences.zh: 但就像对待卢梭和伏尔泰一样，他的怀疑逐渐被博斯韦尔的魅力所融化。

sentences.en: And before long, as ever, Boswell is getting on with Paoli tremendously well.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，一如既往，博斯韦尔和保利相处得非常好。

sentences.en: And Boswell stays with Paoli for two months.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔在保利那里待了两个月。

sentences.en: And as they part, after this two-month stay, Paoli takes him by the hand and shakes it, as Paoli says, as a friend.
sentences.zh: 当他们分开时，在两个月的逗留之后，保利拉着他的手摇了摇，正如保利所说，像朋友一样。

sentences.en: Oh, Boswell couldn't be more delighted at this.
sentences.zh: 噢，博斯韦尔对此感到无比高兴。

sentences.en: I dare not transcribe from my private notes the feelings which I had at this interview.
sentences.zh: 我不敢从我的私人笔记中摘录我在这次会面时的感受。

sentences.en: I should perhaps appear too enthusiastic.
sentences.zh: 我可能会显得太狂热了。

sentences.en: So if Boswell is nervous about seeming too enthusiastic, I mean, he must be about to explode.
sentences.zh: 所以如果博斯韦尔担心显得太狂热，那他肯定快要爆炸了。

sentences.en: And so he returns to Italy absolutely aglow with zeal for the Corsican cause.
sentences.zh: 于是他回到意大利，对科西嘉事业充满了热情。

sentences.en: And I would say that Boswell is probably the first in a long line of Europeans who travel to the scene of a freedom fight and come back absolutely enamored with it.
sentences.zh: 我想说，博斯韦尔可能是欧洲人中第一批前往自由斗争现场，并对之完全着迷的人。

sentences.en: You said he's like Che Guevara.
sentences.zh: 你说他像切·格瓦拉。

sentences.en: I mean, Boswell would absolutely, you know, have put up a Che Guevara poster.
sentences.zh: 我是说，博斯韦尔绝对会挂一张切·格瓦拉的海报。

sentences.en: That's what he's all about.
sentences.zh: 他就是那种人。

sentences.en: But actually, I mean, he goes much further than that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他做得远不止于此。

sentences.en: So he's, while he, I mean, again, this is quite student on a gap year-ish.
sentences.zh: 当他——这又有点像间隔年的学生。

sentences.en: He returns from the island with a full outfit of Corsican clothes.
sentences.zh: 他从岛上回来时，穿了一整套科西嘉服装。

sentences.en: And Paoli has given him a pair of pistols.
sentences.zh: 保利还送了他一把手枪。

sentences.en: So he's got those as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他也有了那些东西。

sentences.en: He must look absolutely ridiculous walking around London, these Corsican trousers weighed with his pistols.
sentences.zh: 他穿着科西嘉裤子，别着手枪在伦敦走来走去，看起来一定非常滑稽。

sentences.en: Well, we will see.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们会看到的。

sentences.en: He does unfurl his Corsican costume when he's back in England in due course.
sentences.zh: 他回到英国后，适时地展示了他的科西嘉服装。

sentences.en: When he's returned from Corsica, he's on the continent.
sentences.zh: 当他从科西嘉回来时，他还在欧洲大陆。

sentences.en: He starts writing unsigned letters to English newspapers, talking about Boswell in the third person,
sentences.zh: 他开始给英国报纸写匿名信，以第三人称谈论博斯韦尔，

sentences.en: hinting that he's been to Corsica on a kind of secret mission on behalf of the British government.
sentences.zh: 暗示他曾代表英国政府去科西嘉执行某种秘密任务。

sentences.en: And his aim in doing this is to whip up interest in Britain on behalf of Corsican independence, to try and pressure the British government to swing behind Paoli, you know,
sentences.zh: 他这样做的目的是为了在英国激起人们对科西嘉独立的兴趣，试图向英国政府施压，支持保利，你知道，

sentences.en: to kind of back him.
sentences.zh: 去支持他。

sentences.en: It's a bit like, I suppose, you know, people in America trying to get Trump to back Zelensky.
sentences.zh: 这有点像，我想，美国人试图让特朗普支持泽连斯基。

sentences.en: It's that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种事。

sentences.en: But also, of course, it's always to a degree about Boswell himself.
sentences.zh: 但当然，在某种程度上，这总是关于博斯韦尔自己。

sentences.en: He's trying to present himself in these letters as a kind of a man of mystery.
sentences.zh: 他试图在这些信件中把自己塑造成一个神秘人物。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's the kind of man who would – I can picture him walking across Afghanistan and then writing a book about it.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是那种——我能想象他走过阿富汗，然后写一本书。

sentences.en: Can you picture that?
sentences.zh: 你能想象吗？

sentences.en: This has been hanging over the story from the beginning, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 这件事从一开始就笼罩在这个故事里，不是吗？

sentences.en: The Alistair Campbell, Roy Stewart, Dr. Johnson, Boswell parallels.
sentences.zh: 阿拉斯泰尔·坎贝尔、罗里·斯图尔特、约翰逊博士和博斯韦尔之间的相似之处。

sentences.en: Well, perhaps in build.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许在体格上。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, what I will say about Boswell is that he is much, much readier to confess in every lurid detail everything that he's thinking and doing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于博斯韦尔，我想说的是，他更愿意坦白他所想和所做的一切，包括每一个细节。

sentences.en: Than Rory.
sentences.zh: 比罗里更愿意。

sentences.en: Well, I think than pretty much anyone today, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，老实说，我觉得比今天几乎任何人都愿意。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Boswell is now returning home because Lord Affleck, I mean, absolutely dyspeptic by this point, has sent him a letter saying, come back.
sentences.zh: 总之，博斯韦尔现在要回家了，因为阿弗莱克勋爵——此时已经完全消化不良了——给他发了一封信说：回来。

sentences.en: Don't bother seeing anything in France.
sentences.zh: 别费心去法国看什么了。

sentences.en: There is nothing to be learned by travelling in France.
sentences.zh: 在法国旅行学不到任何东西。

sentences.en: He knows he's been there.
sentences.zh: 他知道，他去过那里。

sentences.en: And so Boswell heads back.
sentences.zh: 于是博斯韦尔回去了。

sentences.en: He's had this brilliant time.
sentences.zh: 他度过了一段精彩的时光。

sentences.en: He's been hanging out with Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 他和卢梭混在一起。

sentences.en: He's been hanging out with Voltaire.
sentences.zh: 他和伏尔泰混在一起。

sentences.en: He's been a freedom fighter in Corsica.
sentences.zh: 他在科西嘉当过自由战士。

sentences.en: And now he has – you know, he faces the prospect of returning home and becoming an Edinburgh lawyer.
sentences.zh: 而现在他面临着回国成为爱丁堡律师的前景。

sentences.en: However, on the bright side, going back to Britain does have one positive.
sentences.zh: 然而，从好的一面来看，回到英国确实有一个积极因素。

sentences.en: And that positive, of course, is Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 那个积极因素，当然就是塞缪尔·约翰逊。

sentences.en: And Boswell has not forgotten Johnson while he was on his travels.
sentences.zh: 博斯韦尔在旅行时并没有忘记约翰逊。

sentences.en: He's thrilled to have met Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 他很高兴见到卢梭。

sentences.en: He's thrilled to have met Voltaire.
sentences.zh: 他很高兴见到伏尔泰。

sentences.en: But the whole way through, Johnson remains Boswell's moral touchstone.
sentences.zh: 但自始至终，约翰逊一直是博斯韦尔的道德试金石。

sentences.en: And throughout his journals, whenever he feels that he's slumping into depression or he's tempted to, you know, go out on the streets spending money on prostitutes,
sentences.zh: 在他的日记中，每当他感到陷入抑郁，或者想去街上花钱找妓女时，

sentences.en: he kind of reins himself in by saying, resemble Johnson, your mind will strengthen.
sentences.zh: 他就会通过对自己说“像约翰逊一样，你的思想就会变得强大”来约束自己。

sentences.en: And this is kind of – you know, he's always telling himself, be like Johnson.
sentences.zh: 这就是——他总是告诉自己：要像约翰逊一样。

sentences.en: Do what Johnson would do.
sentences.zh: 做约翰逊会做的事。

sentences.en: And he's kind of pumping these kind of staccato imperatives.
sentences.zh: 他一直在给自己灌输这些断断续续的命令。

sentences.en: He has done what Dr. Johnson has done because ever since he left Johnson at Harwich, he has been able to fend off the foul feed of the genitals, no?
sentences.zh: 他做到了约翰逊博士所做的事，因为自从他在哈里奇离开约翰逊以来，他一直能够抵御生殖器的污秽冲动，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, he had in Holland, which is one of the reasons why he was so depressed, and in Germany, and in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他在荷兰时有过，这也是他如此抑郁的原因之一，在德国和瑞士也是如此。

sentences.en: When he talks to Rousseau, it's obvious that he has been trying to think of a way to square the circle.
sentences.zh: 当他与卢梭交谈时，很明显他一直在想办法解决这个矛盾。

sentences.en: How can you have lots of sex with multiple women while remaining a Christian?
sentences.zh: 如何在保持基督徒身份的同时，与多个女性发生性关系？

sentences.en: And so he points out to Rousseau that in Genesis, the biblical patriarchs seem to have had lots of concubines.
sentences.zh: 于是他向卢梭指出，在《创世记》中，圣经里的族长们似乎有很多妾。

sentences.en: And so he says to Rousseau, well, wouldn't this be a possibility?
sentences.zh: 所以他问卢梭：难道这不可能吗？

sentences.en: I mean, couldn't I just keep a harem like Abraham did?
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不能像亚伯拉罕那样养个后宫吗？

sentences.en: And he's obviously hoping that Rousseau will back him on this.
sentences.zh: 显然，他希望卢梭能在这一点上支持他。

sentences.en: And Rousseau does not, actually.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，卢梭并没有。

sentences.en: So he's a bit disappointed by that.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此感到有些失望。

sentences.en: And then I said he arrives in Italy and misbehaves.
sentences.zh: 然后我说他到了意大利，就开始胡作非为。

sentences.en: I mean, he cracks very, very badly.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他堕落得非常、非常厉害。

sentences.en: So in Naples, he'd written, I was truly libertine.
sentences.zh: 他在那不勒斯写道：我真是个浪荡子。

sentences.en: I ran after girls without restraint.
sentences.zh: 我毫无节制地追逐女孩。

sentences.en: And in Rome, he writes to Rousseau, I sallied forth of an evening like an imperious lion.
sentences.zh: 而在罗马，他写信给卢梭说：我像一头威风凛凛的狮子一样在夜晚出没。

sentences.en: He says, the sun is hot.
sentences.zh: 他说，阳光很炽热。

sentences.en: It's inflamed my blood.
sentences.zh: 它点燃了我的血液。

sentences.en: I can't help myself.
sentences.zh: 我无法自控。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What about Paris?
sentences.zh: 那巴黎呢？

sentences.en: So he gets to Paris.
sentences.zh: 于是他到了巴黎。

sentences.en: Does he behave himself in Paris?
sentences.zh: 他在巴黎安分守己了吗？

sentences.en: So this is 1766.
He's 26 years old, all right?
sentences.zh: 他当时26岁，明白吗？

sentences.en: He's about to turn 26.
sentences.zh: 他快满26岁了。

sentences.en: No, he doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，他没有。

sentences.en: And in fact, things take a very dark turn because he's been in Paris a week or so.
sentences.zh: 事实上，情况变得非常糟糕，因为他到巴黎才一周左右。

sentences.en: And he picks up a Scottish newspaper that he finds there.
sentences.zh: 他随手拿起一份在那里找到的苏格兰报纸。

sentences.en: And he reads to his horror that his mother is dead.
sentences.zh: 他惊恐地读到，他的母亲去世了。

sentences.en: And he'd loved his mother.
sentences.zh: 他曾经很爱他的母亲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So he's devastated by this.
sentences.zh: 所以他对此感到悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And so he vents this feeling of despair in a classic Boswell way by going to a brothel.
sentences.zh: 于是，他以典型的鲍斯威尔方式，通过去妓院来宣泄这种绝望感。

sentences.en: That's how he copes with it.
sentences.zh: 这就是他应对的方式。

sentences.en: Of course he does.
sentences.zh: 他当然会这么做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Also in Paris, amazingly, is Rousseau's mistress, Therese Le Vasseur, who we last met in Switzerland.
sentences.zh: 令人惊讶的是，卢梭的情妇泰蕾兹·勒瓦瑟当时也在巴黎，我们上次在瑞士见过她。

sentences.en: And she is in Paris because she is heading on to England and specifically to Chiswick in West London, where Rousseau has settled.
sentences.zh: 她之所以在巴黎，是因为她正准备前往英国，具体来说是去伦敦西部的奇西克，卢梭在那里定居了。

sentences.en: And the reason that he's settled there is that he's been driven out of Switzerland by outraged locals.
sentences.zh: 他之所以定居在那里，是因为他被愤怒的当地人赶出了瑞士。

sentences.en: And the principal reason for their outrage is the fact that Rousseau, a man who, as we mentioned, is very keen and insistent on good parenting,
sentences.zh: 他们愤怒的主要原因是，卢梭这个我们提到过非常热衷并坚持良好育儿观念的人，

sentences.en: has recently been outed as having had these five children by his mistress and dumping them all in an orphanage.
sentences.zh: 最近被曝光与情妇生了五个孩子，并把他们全都扔进了孤儿院。

sentences.en: Don't tell me that Rousseau, of all people, has been exposed as a hypocrite.
sentences.zh: 别告诉我，卢梭竟然被揭露是个伪君子。

sentences.en: And so he's been driven out of Switzerland and he's gone to take refuge in England.
sentences.zh: 所以他被赶出了瑞士，去英国避难了。

sentences.en: And Therese is now travelling there to join him.
sentences.zh: 而泰蕾兹现在正前往那里与他团聚。

sentences.en: And so Rousseau has asked Boswell, will you escort Therese and bring her to me?
sentences.zh: 于是卢梭请求鲍斯威尔：你能护送泰蕾兹并把她带给我吗？

sentences.en: And Boswell does.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯威尔照做了。

sentences.en: And inevitably they have sex.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，他们发生了关系。

sentences.en: Initially, Boswell can't perform because he's so nervous about having sex with Rousseau's mistress.
sentences.zh: 起初，鲍斯威尔因为和卢梭的情妇发生关系而感到非常紧张，无法表现。

sentences.en: But then he manages it, goes in hard.
sentences.zh: 但后来他成功了，表现得很卖力。

sentences.en: So Therese says, listen, I'll give you some lessons.
sentences.zh: 于是泰蕾兹说：听着，我来教你几招。

sentences.en: And so they have 12 lessons on the journey from Paris to Dover.
sentences.zh: 于是他们在从巴黎到多佛的旅途中上了12节课。

sentences.en: And Therese is incredibly pleased with herself.
sentences.zh: 泰蕾兹对自己感到非常满意。

sentences.en: Boswell finds it really dull and he gallantly compares Therese to a bad rider galloping downhill.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯威尔觉得这真的很无聊，他甚至绅士地把泰蕾兹比作一个下坡时骑术不佳的骑手。

sentences.en: So neither is satisfied.
sentences.zh: 所以两人都不满意。

sentences.en: Both of them have let themselves down.
sentences.zh: 他们都让自己失望了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it's probably with some relief that Boswell drops Therese off with Rousseau in Chiswick and then goes rushing off to be reunited with Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 所以，鲍斯威尔把泰蕾兹送到奇西克交给卢梭，然后匆忙赶去与塞缪尔·约翰逊团聚，这大概让他松了一口气。

sentences.en: Well, you could never accuse Dr. Johnson of being either too flaccid or lacking art, could you?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你永远不能指责约翰逊博士过于软弱或缺乏艺术感，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got all the arts.
sentences.zh: 他拥有所有的艺术天赋。

sentences.en: He has.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And also he has this human kindness beneath his bearish exterior.
sentences.zh: 而且在他那粗犷的外表下，还有着这种人性的善良。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And he's delighted to see Boswell and greets him with much kindness, Boswell says.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯威尔说，他很高兴见到鲍斯威尔，并以极大的善意迎接了他。

sentences.en: But at the same time, Johnson is bearish.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，约翰逊也是个粗人。

sentences.en: He gives Boswell the occasional mauling.
sentences.zh: 他偶尔会把鲍斯威尔训斥一顿。

sentences.en: Boswell is talking all about his holidays and going on about how he's met Rousseau.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯威尔一直在谈论他的假期，喋喋不休地说他如何见到了卢梭。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Johnson explodes.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊爆发了。

sentences.en: I mean, Rousseau is so not Samuel Johnson.
sentences.zh: 我是说，卢梭根本不是塞缪尔·约翰逊那种人。

sentences.en: So he says, Rousseau, sir, is a very bad man.
sentences.zh: 所以他说：先生，卢梭是个非常糟糕的人。

sentences.en: I would sooner sign a sentence for his transportation than that of any felon who has gone from the old Bailey these many years.
sentences.zh: 比起这些年来从老贝利法院走出的任何重罪犯，我宁愿签署将他流放的判决书。

sentences.en: Yes, I should like to have him work in the plantations.
sentences.zh: 是的，我真想让他去种植园干活。

sentences.en: To which Boswell, who's become very good at basically kind of coaxing Johnson along so that he'll come out with ever more outrageous statements, says,
sentences.zh: 对此，鲍斯威尔——他已经非常擅长诱导约翰逊，让他说出更离谱的言论——说道：

sentences.en: Sir, do you think Rousseau is bad a man as Voltaire?
sentences.zh: 先生，您认为卢梭和伏尔泰一样坏吗？

sentences.en: To which Johnson replies, why, sir, it is difficult to settle the proportion of iniquity between them.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊回答说：哎呀，先生，很难确定他们之间罪恶的比例。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Dr. Johnson, I think I said this in the last episode, he would have made a tremendous columnist for the Daily Express.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊博士，我想我在上一集说过，他会成为《每日快报》的一名出色的专栏作家。

sentences.en: He does a wonderful podcast, isn't he, I think?
sentences.zh: 我想他会做一个很棒的播客，不是吗？

sentences.en: A very splenetic podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 一个非常刻薄的播客。

sentences.en: Oh, completely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: He'd be robust in his views.
sentences.zh: 他的观点会很强硬。

sentences.en: I mean, no question.
sentences.zh: 我是说，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Well, and so, I mean, as an example of this, Boswell, after Johnson has dismissed Voltaire, then tries one of Voltaire's infidel sallies on Johnson, to which Johnson responds,
sentences.zh: 嗯，举个例子，鲍斯威尔在约翰逊驳斥了伏尔泰之后，又试图在约翰逊面前卖弄伏尔泰的那些异端邪说，约翰逊回应道：

sentences.en: This now is such stuff as I used to talk to my mother when I first began to think myself a clever fellow, and she ought to have whipped me for it.
sentences.zh: 这简直是我刚开始自以为聪明时对母亲说的话，她本该为此狠狠抽我一顿。

sentences.en: So he basically thinks that Voltaire's a teenager.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上认为伏尔泰是个青少年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And then Boswell starts moaning on about how he's got to become a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 然后鲍斯威尔开始抱怨他必须成为一名律师。

sentences.en: He defines being a lawyer as being excelled by plodding blockheads.
sentences.zh: 他把当律师定义为被那些平庸的笨蛋所超越。

sentences.en: So I don't know what our legal listeners will make of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道我们的法律界听众会怎么看这一点。

sentences.en: And Johnson, again, he has no time for this now, for any self-pity.
sentences.zh: 而约翰逊，同样，他现在没时间理会这些自怜自艾。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He tells Boswell to man up.
sentences.zh: 他告诉鲍斯威尔要像个男人一样振作起来。

sentences.en: Yeah, but, I mean, Boswell does have to man up now, because the legal hell is opening up before him.
sentences.zh: 是啊，但是，我是说，鲍斯威尔现在确实必须振作起来，因为法律的地狱正在他面前开启。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, from this point on, Boswell is going to be locked into a legal career.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从这一点开始，鲍斯威尔将被锁定在法律职业生涯中。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: There's going to be no more tazzing around Corsica or meeting infidel philosophers.
sentences.zh: 再也不会有在科西嘉岛闲逛或会见异端哲学家的事情了。

sentences.en: So he heads back to Scotland.
sentences.zh: 于是他回到了苏格兰。

sentences.en: He's been away for three and a half years.
sentences.zh: 他已经离开三年半了。

sentences.en: But from now on, you know, his job is going to be to practice as an advocate.
sentences.zh: 但从现在起，你知道，他的工作将是作为一名辩护律师执业。

sentences.en: And he does it regularly.
sentences.zh: 而且他做得很有规律。

sentences.en: He does it reliably.
sentences.zh: 他做得非常可靠。

sentences.en: He's actually quite good at it.
sentences.zh: 他其实做得相当不错。

sentences.en: So I think it helps that actually in Scotland, the Court of Sessions, before which Boswell is appearing as an advocate, it only sits for six months a year.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这有帮助，实际上在苏格兰，鲍斯威尔作为辩护律师出庭的最高法院每年只开庭六个月。

sentences.en: So that gives Boswell quite a lot of time to do other things, sue other interests, other dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 所以这给了鲍斯威尔很多时间去做其他事情，追求其他兴趣，其他梦想。

sentences.en: And the most public of these remains his activism on behalf of Corsican independence.
sentences.zh: 而其中最公开的仍然是他为科西嘉独立所做的活动。

sentences.en: So he gets back.
sentences.zh: 所以他回来了。

sentences.en: He hasn't forgotten Corsica.
sentences.zh: 他没有忘记科西嘉。

sentences.en: And to give him credit, he makes representations to various British ministers, including William Pitt, the elder, who's a very significant player.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，他向包括老威廉·皮特在内的几位英国大臣进行了陈述，皮特是一个非常重要的人物。

sentences.en: And Pitt says, yeah, I'll see what I can do.
sentences.zh: 皮特说：好的，我会看看我能做什么。

sentences.en: And, of course, does nothing.
sentences.zh: 当然，他什么也没做。

sentences.en: Boswell also, he writes up his travels in Corsica as a book.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯威尔还把他科西嘉的旅行写成了一本书。

sentences.en: And it's published.
sentences.zh: 书出版了。

sentences.en: And it's a great success.
sentences.zh: 而且非常成功。

sentences.en: And it wins him the nickname of Corsica Boswell, which he absolutely loves.
sentences.zh: 这为他赢得了科西嘉·鲍斯威尔的绰号，他对此非常喜欢。

sentences.en: And he writes about it in his journal.
sentences.zh: 他在日记中写到了这件事。

sentences.en: It is fine to have such a character as I have.
sentences.zh: 拥有我这样的性格真好。

sentences.en: I enjoy it much.
sentences.zh: 我很享受它。

sentences.en: He's very pleased with himself.
sentences.zh: 他对自己非常满意。

sentences.en: And, Dominic, you asked about this outfit of Corsican clothes that he's brought back with him.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，你问过他带回来的那套科西嘉服装。

sentences.en: And does he ever wear it?
sentences.zh: 他穿过吗？

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他穿过。

sentences.en: And the opportunity comes in September 1769, Johnson's old friend David Garrick, the greatest actor of his day, the greatest Shakespearean actor of his day,
sentences.zh: 机会出现在1769年9月，约翰逊的老朋友大卫·加里克，当时最伟大的演员，当时最伟大的莎士比亚剧演员，

sentences.en: stages a Shakespeare jubilee in Stratford-upon-Avon, Shakespeare's birthplace.
sentences.zh: 在莎士比亚的出生地埃文河畔斯特拉特福举办了一场莎士比亚纪念庆典。

sentences.en: Oh, nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，不错。

sentences.en: And it's going to be a great celebration of the Bard, and it's scheduled to last for three days.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场对这位吟游诗人的盛大庆祝活动，计划持续三天。

sentences.en: And, in fact, it has an enormous impact in kind of what becomes bardolatry, this notion of Shakespeare as the supreme genius.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它对后来所谓的莎士比亚崇拜——即莎士比亚是至高无上的天才这一观念——产生了巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Garrick's jubilee plays a key role in that, despite the fact that actually it's all – I mean, it's literally a washout.

sentences.en: Because on the second day, so much rain falls that the third day simply has to be cancelled.
sentences.zh: 因为第二天雨下得太大，第三天的活动不得不取消。

sentences.en: And everyone's kind of tramping around in mud, the tarpaulins fall down, all of that, you know, the live shows have to be cancelled.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在泥泞中跋涉，防水布倒塌了，所有这些，你知道，现场表演不得不取消。

sentences.en: But Boswell, who has gone there, has a lovely time because he has turned up in his Corsican costume.
sentences.zh: 但去了那里的鲍斯威尔却玩得很开心，因为他穿着他的科西嘉服装出现了。

sentences.en: And there he is with his guns and his, you know, sash and all that kind of stuff.

sentences.zh: 我是说，非常具有拜伦式的先驱风范。

sentences.en: And he reads out a poem that he has written himself about Corsican liberty, and he wrote about it, I was as much a favourite as I could desire.

sentences.en: In other words, Shakespeare jubilee's a washout, but Boswell's been brilliant.

sentences.en: Of course.

sentences.en: Of course he has.
sentences.zh: 他当然表现出色。

sentences.en: So there are only two shadows on this kind of Corsica-Boswell heaven.

sentences.en: The first is that actually the dream of Corsican liberty is conclusively over now, because Jenner is no longer the mistress of Corsica, because the French have now invaded.
sentences.zh: 第一是科西嘉自由的梦想现在已经彻底破灭了，因为詹纳不再是科西嘉的主人，因为法国人已经入侵了。

sentences.en: And of course, this is now, you know, this is crucial, because this explains why in the long run, Napoleon, a Corsican will end up emperor of the French.
sentences.zh: 当然，这现在至关重要，因为这解释了为什么从长远来看，科西嘉人拿破仑最终会成为法国皇帝。

sentences.en: So it's a momentous development.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个重大的发展。

sentences.en: And poor General Paoli, he has to flee, he goes into exile, and he turns up in London a few days after the jubilee to claim political asylum.

sentences.en: Boswell, again, to give him credit, he's really good.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯威尔，平心而论，他真的很棒。

sentences.zh: 他把保利介绍给约翰逊和他的所有朋友，以及他能介绍的所有人。

sentences.en: And Paoli remains, I think, the kind of the purest hero in Boswell's pantheon, because

sentences.en: What does Johnson say?
sentences.zh: 约翰逊说了什么？

sentences.zh: 清空你脑子里的科西嘉，我想它占据的时间太长了。

sentences.en: So I'm giving him the proper Midlands accent that he would have had.
sentences.zh: 所以我用他本该有的地道的米德兰口音来表达。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.en: Shut up about Corsica.
sentences.zh: 闭嘴，别再提科西嘉了。

sentences.en: But Boswell knows that this kind of abrasiveness, you know, it comes with the territory.
sentences.zh: 但鲍斯威尔知道这种尖刻，你知道，这是必然的。

sentences.zh: 关于鲍斯韦尔在莎士比亚禧年庆典前一年写下的那段精彩记述，还有一件事。

sentences.zh: 禧年庆典。

sentences.zh: 鲍斯韦尔曾与约翰逊及其他几位友人在河岸街的一家酒馆——“皇冠与锚”共进晚餐。

sentences.zh: 那天整个晚上，约翰逊都表现得格外狂放不羁。

sentences.zh: 但约翰逊其实并没有怎么驳斥鲍斯韦尔，对吧？

sentences.zh: 因为他们始终是莫逆之交。

sentences.zh: 而且他们之间有一种深厚的情谊，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 如果约翰逊觉得鲍斯韦尔该骂，他确实会毫不留情地驳斥他。

sentences.en: But he's always ready to show Boswell that he loves him.
sentences.zh: 但他总是乐于向鲍斯韦尔表达自己的关爱。

sentences.en: Johnson can tell that Boswell not only loves him, but reveres him.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊看得出来，鲍斯韦尔不仅爱他，而且敬重他。

sentences.en: And Johnson is human and he likes this.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊也是凡人，他很受用这一点。

sentences.en: Even after Boswell gets married in 1769, he can't bear to kind of abandon Johnson, to abandon
sentences.zh: 即使在1769年结婚后，鲍斯韦尔也无法忍受离开约翰逊，离开

sentences.en: And so he makes these regular trips down to the capital.
sentences.zh: 所以他还是会定期前往首都。

sentences.en: He feels a bit guilty about it, but not guilty enough to stop doing it.
sentences.zh: 他对此感到有些愧疚，但还没到让他停止这种行为的地步。

sentences.en: And Boswell's friendship with Johnson means that even though he's now a Scottish lawyer, he does kind of remain at the heart of London literary life.
sentences.zh: 鲍斯韦尔与约翰逊的友谊意味着，尽管他现在是一名苏格兰律师，但他依然处于伦敦文学生活的核心。

sentences.en: This continues to make Boswell unbelievably happy.
sentences.zh: 这让鲍斯韦尔感到无比幸福。

sentences.en: So there's a kind of wonderful moment in 1772.
sentences.zh: 1772年发生了一件美妙的事情。

sentences.zh: 他当时正和约翰逊以及约翰逊的朋友奥利弗·戈德史密斯坐在一起，后者是一位非常著名的

sentences.zh: 爱尔兰诗人、小说家和剧作家。

sentences.en: She stoops to conquer.
sentences.zh: 《屈身求爱》的作者。

sentences.zh: 就像他对待卢梭和伏尔泰那样，鲍斯韦尔暗自窃喜。

sentences.en: I mean, he says, he writes, he felt a completion of happiness.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他写道，他感到了一种圆满的幸福。

sentences.zh: 我只是坐在那里，在心里暗自欢喜。

sentences.en: I think that's such a great, a great phrase.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这真是一个非常棒的表达。

sentences.en: And the following spring, the seal is set on this kind of sense of, of, of joy of hugging himself in his mind.
sentences.zh: 第二年春天，这种“在心里暗自欢喜”的喜悦感得到了印证。
